summary_paragraph: A man with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, type 2 diabetes, atrial fibrillation, and a history of hyperparathyroidism was admitted for lethargy, nausea, and vomiting. He was found to have hypercalcemia and a supratherapeutic digoxin level, contributing to toxic metabolic encephalopathy. His condition improved with discontinuation of digoxin, increased cinacalcet, and ongoing dialysis. He developed recurrent aspiration pneumonia due to swallowing difficulties, leading to multiple antibiotic courses. Despite medical management, he experienced progressive decline. Goals of care shifted to comfort-focused treatment, with code status changed to DNR/DNI. Two days before death, he developed symptoms of small bowel obstruction, which was managed conservatively. He passed away peacefully with family present, under palliative care.
problems: Pneumonitis due to inhalation of food or vomitus
Cardiotonic glycosides and drugs of similar action causing adverse effects in therapeutic use
Diabetes with neurological manifestations, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
